The core failure mode in maritime MOT is the mismatch between short-term spatial proximity and long-term identity. Classical IoU-based trackers assume that nearby detections in consecutive frames share the same identity, which breaks down when a target moves rapidly out of view. Our solution leverages the fact that a moving object's trajectory in 3D world space follows a predictable kinematic curve given accurate metadata. By transforming both entry and exit detections into a common world coordinate frame, we create a metric that decouples spatial closeness from temporal continuity. This projection acts as a "motion-compensated filter" that aligns predictions across frames despite camera jitter and drone acceleration. Mathematically, it establishes a dual relationship between the observation space (image plane) and the state space (world coordinates), enabling a clean separation of tracking errors due to geometry versus those due to appearance.
